design:
Tier 1: UI import change, one test, one re-measurement; no migration, no Hub-restart hazard (the committed bundle reaches the operator's :8000 app on reload, which is the point; rebuilt with `make ui`).

Decisions (author's choices unless marked):
- Fix the cause rather than raise the ceiling: load the checkpoints screen on demand like every other screen, through lazyScreens.ts, so a loaded one renders without a loading flash (the slice-4 rule).
- The ceiling becomes a test, not a drive: the bundle is committed, so a plain test that reads index.html's entry script and fails over the budget costs milliseconds and runs on every task. The browser drive stays the proof of time and frames; it is too heavy to run per task.
- The drive measures the committed bundle as well as a fresh build (a flag), since the committed bundle is what ships.
- Numbers (usable time, frame bound) are the operator's: see open questions. Budgets remain provisional until used on the work VDI (roadmap).
- No virtualisation: memoisation meets the bound and windowing breaks find-in-page and scroll anchoring. Revisit only if the re-measured dropped frames exceed the bound.

CONTRACT (grounded in scripts/drive/perf_ui_open.py, hub/ui/src/lib/lazyScreens.ts, hub/tests/test_ui_staleness.py):
- No setting, route, response field or event is added or changed.
- Drive: perf_ui_open.py already takes `--ui-dir` (required, line 349) and `--scenario open|stream`, so measuring the committed bundle needs no flag; the extension is a printed line `entry script <file> <bytes> bytes` naming the file index.html loads. Its existing line 'JS before usable' (line 268, unit KB = 1024 bytes, BUDGET["js_kb_before_usable"] = 700) counts all script requested before usable, while the test measures the entry file only: the test is the narrower, per-task guard and the drive the total.
- Screen: `export const CheckpointsScreen = screen(() => import('@/components/checkpoints/CheckpointsScreen'), 'CheckpointsScreen')` in hub/ui/src/lib/lazyScreens.ts beside the others (lines 48-63), imported by App.tsx from '@/lib/lazyScreens' in place of line 49. The factory returns the loaded component with no Suspense fallback once loaded; loadAllScreens() loads it with the others.
- Test: hub/tests/test_ui_entry_budget.py with `ENTRY_CEILING_BYTES = 700 * 1024`, `entry_script(ui_dir: Path) -> Path` (the module script in `<ui_dir>/index.html`), and `check_entry(ui_dir, ceiling_bytes)`, which raises AssertionError with the message `<file name> is <size> bytes, over the <ceiling> byte ceiling`. A second test fails when the entry contains the markers `react-markdown` or `micromark`.
- Existing guards the change meets, none relaxed: UI tests that render App must `await loadAllScreens()` first (hub/ui/src/__tests__/checkpointsTab.test.tsx does); hub/tests/test_ui_staleness.py and test_ui_build_stamp.py require the committed bundle and source to agree, so lazyScreens.ts, App.tsx and hub/hub/static/ui change in one commit.
- Task status path: none walked; the drive uses real agent turns only for the stream scenario, bound to Haiku.

limits: The acceptance drive is proposed coverage: it is not run for this document and no figure here is a fresh browser measurement; the only figures measured now are file sizes.
The cause of the +207 KB is read from source and from the entry's contents, not bisected by building each commit.
A 6x CPU throttle on this machine is an estimate of the work VDI, not a measurement of it.
Frames are measured in headless Chromium; a real GPU-composited window may differ.

open_questions.question: What is the stated time for the project screen to be usable at a 6x-throttled CPU? Options: 4.0 s (the current budget; 2.85 s measured on 2026-10-25), 3.0 s (tighter, margin only 0.15 s on that measurement), or wait for real work-VDI use. Recommendation: keep 4.0 s; tighten once the VDI has been used.

What dropped-frame bound for a 1,000-row conversation streaming 90 lines a minute? Options: 10% (current; measured 8.7%, thin margin), 15% (safer for noise, looser), or 8% (would fail today's measurement). Recommendation: keep 10% and have the drive take the worst of three runs, reporting the margin.

What ceiling for script loaded before usable? Options: 700 KB (current), or 650 KB to keep a margin over the ~610 KB the entry returns to. Recommendation: 700 KB, so ordinary additions are not blocked while a 200 KB import still is.

Should the browser drive ever run automatically (nightly or per release)? Options: never (size test only), nightly on this machine, or on every UI change. Recommendation: size test per task now; the drive by hand before a release, as today.

The size test measures the entry file only, while the ceiling in the requirement and the drive count all script loaded before usable. A future import that lands in a separate eagerly loaded chunk would pass the test and fail the drive. Options: (a) test the entry file only (this document); (b) also sum the modulepreload links in index.html. Recommendation: (b) if the build emits preloads for such chunks, confirmed in the size-test task; otherwise (a).

problem:
**What was built.** Commit a8f2015 (2026-10-25, merged in 08a7c2c) made the sidebar's per-project listings one request, split every screen but the Overview into its own chunk (hub/ui/src/lib/lazyScreens.ts:1-86, prefetched one per idle period at hub/ui/src/App.tsx:166), and memoised the timeline so a streamed line re-renders only its own turn (hub/ui/src/lib/agentTimelineModel.ts:88 `reuseTurns`; hub/ui/src/components/agents/AgentTimeline.tsx:435-438 `TurnSection` memo). Its drive, scripts/drive/perf_ui_open.py, passed at a 6x-throttled CPU: 14 API requests (budget 15), 565 KB of script before usable (700), usable in 2.85 s (4.0), 8.7% dropped frames (10), longest task 75 ms (150), 13.5 ms of long task per line (40).

**What has happened since.** The committed entry script hub/hub/static/ui/assets/index-lsIeO-UK.js is 823,082 bytes (254,383 gzip); the whole bundle is 2,048,920 bytes (602,950 gzip). Its size by committed bundle: 578 KB on 2026-10-26 (ef6647c), 609 KB on 2026-11-03, then 816 KB at 63924a2 (2026-11-04, ECFR-5), 823 KB now. That step is +207 KB. The cause visible in source: the checkpoints screen added in that commit is imported directly in the first script (hub/ui/src/App.tsx:49, rendered at :575), not through lazyScreens.ts, and it brings the markdown and code-highlight stack (the entry now contains react-markdown and micromark) that slice 4 had moved out. 823 KB is over the 700 KB ceiling (BUDGET `js_kb_before_usable`, scripts/drive/perf_ui_open.py:60), and on the operator's weak work machine script time is the dominant open cost (2.79 s of ScriptDuration at the slice's baseline of 1.5 MB, 1.16 s at 565 KB).

**Why nobody noticed.** No test, check or CI step runs perf_ui_open.py or reads the bundle's size (searched .github, scripts/checks, tests, hub/tests). The drive is operator-run by hand, and it builds the source to a temp directory rather than measuring what the Hub ships.

**What is not wrong.** The conversation is not virtualised: every turn is in the DOM (no windowing in hub/ui/src; package.json has no virtualisation library). It is kept smooth by memoisation instead, and that held at 8.7% dropped frames, which leaves little margin under the 10% bound. Request count on open: no project-screen query polls on a timer except the manager's 10 s refetch when a manager exists (hub/ui/src/api/manager.ts:93,237); the rest follow the event stream.

requirements.rationale: Script time is the largest part of a weak machine's open cost: 1.16 s of script at 565 KB, 2.79 s at 1.5 MB.
requirements.statement: The JavaScript the app loads before the project screen is usable totals no more than the stated ceiling (recommended 700 KB uncompressed), measured on the committed bundle in hub/hub/static/ui; today it is 823 KB in the entry script alone.

requirements.rationale: This import is the identified cause of the +207 KB.
requirements.statement: The checkpoints screen loads when it is first opened or when the idle prefetch reaches it, not in the first script; once loaded it draws at once with no loading placeholder, as the other screens do, and the markdown and code-highlight libraries are not part of the entry script.

requirements.rationale: The regression sat unnoticed for three days because nothing measured it.
requirements.statement: A check that runs with the project's ordinary tests fails when the committed entry script (named by hub/hub/static/ui/index.html) exceeds the ceiling, and its message names the entry file, its size and the ceiling.

requirements.rationale: Slice 4 reached 14; this guards it against the same drift.
requirements.statement: Opening a project with 25 projects in the sidebar issues no more than 15 API GET requests from navigation until 3 seconds after the screen is usable, and the 25 conversation listings leave as one request.

requirements.rationale: This is the roadmap's 'usable within a stated time'.
requirements.statement: At a 6x-throttled CPU the project screen (top bar, project rail and the Overview's agent cards) is usable within the stated time (recommended 4.0 s) of navigation, on the committed bundle.

requirements.rationale: This is the roadmap's 'does not drop frames beyond a stated bound'; the recorded margin was 8.7% against 10%.
requirements.statement: With a 1,000-row conversation open at a 6x-throttled CPU and 90 lines a minute arriving, dropped frames stay within the stated bound (recommended 10%), no main-thread task exceeds 150 ms, and long-task time stays within 40 ms per line.

The drive's measurements on the current build, with the previous (2026-10-25) figures beside them, are recorded where the operator reads them, so the budgets can be set from data when the work VDI has been used.

in_scope: The size of the script the app loads before a project screen is usable
A check that keeps that size from growing unnoticed
Re-measuring open time, request count and streaming smoothness on the current build, at a 6x-throttled CPU
non_goals: Changing what any screen shows or does
Server-side cost of routes, git or the database (the other three slices of the roadmap)
Tuning for any machine other than by the 6x throttle (real work-VDI numbers come from the operator's use)
Splitting the stylesheet (293 KB, kept as one file for cascade order, vite.config.ts)
Running the browser drive in CI

summary: The roadmap's fourth slice was built on 2026-10-25 (the app opened in 14 requests and a 565 KB script; a 1,000-row conversation streamed at 8.7% dropped frames) but has since regressed: the committed first script is 823 KB, over the 700 KB budget it set, because a screen added on 2026-11-04 is imported into it. Nothing runs the slice's drive, so nothing noticed. This change puts the first script back under its ceiling, makes that ceiling a check that runs with the tests, and re-records the slice's numbers on the current build so the figures the operator holds are current, not three weeks old.
